transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (Atlas Retail - Head of ML), Lina Gomez (Atlas - Platform Eng), Eric Wu (Atlas - Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — agenda is networking follow-up, result review after the model 2.1 upgrade, tuning KV cache, and then next steps. Anything else from Atlas?
[00:12] Samir: No that's it, mostly the routing surprises I want to make sure we nailed down last week, and the latency numbers after the upgrade.
[00:20] Priya: Cool, I pulled the p99 and p50 traces from the private pilot cluster. We'll run through them, there are a couple spots where cross-AZ egress caused retries.
[00:30] Lina: I left notes in the shared deck about the firewall rules we changed, just to be explicit about the subnets.
[00:36] Jordan: Great. Quick housekeeping: Marco will own the pilot success doc and capture sign-off criteria. Marco you good?
[00:42] Marco: Yep I got it, I'll share a draft after the call.

--- Transcript body ---
[01:15] Priya: Ok starting with the net tests — on Monday we saw 18% packet drops between AZ-a and AZ-b when the collector pod was under load, that triggered our connection pool to fall back to hosted routing which added about 60 to 120 ms of additional latency.
[01:33] Samir: Right and that behavior is what surprised us, because our expectation was the VPC routing should keep it internal, not route out to the public tier.
[01:42] Jordan: There was a misconfiguration in the route table — the egress NACL had a more permissive rule that allowed outbound to the proxy in another region; we caught that and fixed it. Lina, can you confirm the change is in staging?
[01:51] Lina: Confirmed, rule updated. I also pushed a terraform snippet to the repo, see link in chat. The snippet restricts the egress to the specific Redwood ingress IPs and enforces the private route table.
[02:05] Eric: Quick sec — from security side we need the flow logs for at least 30 days and KMS encryption for logs. Are those covered?
[02:13] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS. We have the audit log delivery to S3 in the pilot config; Priya will send the exact IAM policy example.
[02:22] Priya: I'll share the IAM example and the log bucket lifecycle policies after this call.

[03:00] Priya: Moving to model upgrade 2.1 results — we rolled model 2.0 -> 2.1 in canary yesterday. Token-level latency improved slightly, p50 went from 42 ms to 36 ms, but we saw an increase in memory pressure with certain long-context prompts which caused one OOM in the 4-node staging cluster.
[03:20] Samir: The OOM is concerning. What caused the memory spike? We didn't change prompt lengths.
[03:25] Priya: It looks like 2.1 defaults to a different KV cache allocation strategy; the runtime kept larger KV windows for embeddings reranking workloads. We're tuning that now and have a config to reduce the spare KV allocation.
[03:40] Jordan: Can you explain the tradeoff — if we reduce KV allocation do we lose cache hit rate and increase token compute?
[03:47] Priya: Potentially yes, you might see slightly higher per-token compute but it reduces peak memory and prevents OOMs. For the pilot we recommend reducing max KV per shard by 25% and adding more aggressive eviction for low-frequency prefixes.
[03:58] Samir: Ok try that in staging. Also we want to benchmark reranking flows since that's our heavy path.

[05:10] Priya: We ran a reranking bench with 1k queries and saw throughput drop by 8% after reducing KV allocation but tail latency stabilized and no OOMs happened. I'll attach the raw numbers.
[05:25] Samir: That's acceptable if tail latency is stable. We care about p99 more than raw throughput.
[05:31] Jordan: Noted. We'll mark success criteria as p99 < 450 ms on production-like load and no OOMs during 24h soak.

[07:00] Lina: On routing — I ran the canary with the updated route tables and the cross-AZ egress went to zero, but one of the load balancer health checks failed intermittently because of a misconfigured security group referencing an old sg ID.
[07:18] Jordan: That old SG hiccup is why we had a spike. Lina, did you remove the stale rule?
[07:22] Lina: I removed it this morning, health checks are green in staging now.

[09:10] Eric: Security question — for the private deployment do we support SAML SSO and role-based access so that our ops team can access logs but not model endpoints?
[09:20] Jordan: Yes Redwood supports SAML SSO and RBAC at the tenant and route level; we can gate model inference endpoints separately from the console. We'll send the SAML metadata and RBAC examples.
[09:31] Eric: Also need evidence of SOC2 control mapping for audit. Who can provide that?
[09:35] Marco: I'll attach the SOC2 summary and a pointer to the full compliance pack. We may need an NDA for full artifacts.

[12:00] Priya: Back to tuning — batching parameters. We observed that for short prompts batching windows of 10 ms give better throughput without hurting latency. For long-context prompts you want smaller windows to avoid head-of-line delays. We recommend adaptive batching profile: short prompt path uses 12 ms, reranking path uses 6 ms.
[12:24] Samir: Do you have example config we can push via CI?
[12:28] Priya: Yes, Terraform + configmap snippet in the repo. I'll paste after the call.

[15:00] Jordan: Any issues with the on-prem package we gave you? Installer and Helm chart?
[15:07] Lina: Installer worked but we had to bump a kernel setting on two nodes (vm.max_map_count) which wasn't in the installer notes. We added that to our local runbook.
[15:16] Jordan: Thanks, we'll update the docs.

[Crosstalk]
[18:05] Samir: Sorry to jump, are we still planning the benchmark run at load 2x next Tuesday?
[18:10] Marco: Yes still on for 2026-09-15, we're aiming for a 6-hour soak at production-like traffic. Jordan will coordinate.
[18:18] Jordan: I'll send an invite for the benchmark window and runbook.

[20:00] Priya: Small note on cost — with current config and quantization profile the per-token compute cost estimate is about 0.85x of our hosted baseline. If you enable more aggressive int8 fallback you'll save more but with slight quality delta.
[20:18] Samir: We'll want to see quality samples before toggling aggressive quantization. Can you produce a diff on generation quality for key prompt sets?
[20:25] Priya: Yes I'll run the eval suite on the two quant profiles and share the report.

[25:00] Lina: One more network log thing — flow logs were dropping entries when logs hit S3 bucket throttle limits. We raised the S3 request limit and that cleared up. We're still verifying no data loss.
[25:15] Eric: Please capture that in the incident tracker.
[25:20] Lina: Added a note, linking the tracker to the pilot board.

[30:00] Priya: Quick demo of tail traces — sharing my screen. You'll see recovery when a node hits high memory: it routes to healthy nodes, KV eviction occurs, and requests continue but with higher latency for the affected user. The important part is we avoid hard failures.
[30:25] Samir: Ok that matches what we saw in production-like runs, as long as the user-facing retries are within our SLA.

[40:00] Jordan: Let's recap concrete next steps and owners — Marco will draft the pilot success criteria; Jordan will share network diagram and terraform snippet; Priya will run KV cache tuning and quant/quality evals; Lina will validate routing and confirm staging health; Eric will validate SOC2 evidence needs and share specific control numbers.
[40:30] Marco: I'll also list rollback criteria for model upgrades.

[43:00] Samir: Anything blocking our sign-off from security?
[43:06] Eric: We need the SOC2 mapping and the KMS key rotation policy; once we have those we'll run a short security review. Nothing blocking otherwise.

[50:00] Jordan: Great. If nothing else we can close — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts in the next 48 hours.
[50:10] Samir: Thanks all.

End of meeting.
